name: mips_cm_phys_base
prose: Weak function with no arguments (a platform may override it) returning the physical base address of the Coherence Manager GCR block as a phys_addr_t. It returns 0 if read_c0_config() has the MIPS_CONF_M bit clear, or read_c0_config2() has MIPS_CONF_M clear, or read_c0_config3() has MIPS_CONF3_CMGCR clear. Otherwise it reads CMGCRBase with read_c0_cmgcrbase() and returns (cmgcr & MIPS_CMGCRF_BASE) << (36 - 32), i.e. shifted left by 4; the result is 0 if the masked field is 0. It only reads CP0 registers, takes no lock and has no side effects.
note: Reviewer round 15 right that the numeric upper bound in the old prose was wrong (it depended on the width of MIPS_CMGCRF_BASE); the bound and multiple-of-16 claims were removed and the exact expression kept. Slice 185-202.

name: kaslr_disabled
prose: Static inline __init function with no arguments returning true if "nokaslr" is found on the command line in a position that starts a word. If CONFIG_CMDLINE_BOOL is defined it first calls strstr(builtin_cmdline, "nokaslr") on CONFIG_CMDLINE, and returns true if the first occurrence found is at the start of the string or immediately after a space character. Then (always) it calls strstr(arcs_cmdline, "nokaslr") and returns true under the same condition for arcs_cmdline. Otherwise it returns false. Only the first occurrence in each string is examined, so a later occurrence after a space is not seen if an earlier occurrence is not preceded by a space or the start; the text after the match is not checked (so "nokaslrx" also matches). It writes no memory.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (only the first strstr hit is tested), round 2 already covered by the old prose (builtin check has the same boundary rule). Slice cut the head; read relocate.c:243-262 for the declaration and the CONFIG_CMDLINE_BOOL part.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sigaction, int, sig, const struct sigaction __user *, act, struct sigaction __user *, oact)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_sigaction (MIPS, built with CONFIG_TRAD_SIGNALS) taking sig and optional user pointers act and oact. If act is non-NULL: it returns -EFAULT if access_ok(act, sizeof(*act)) fails, or if reading act->sa_handler, act->sa_flags or act->sa_mask.sig[0] with __get_user fails (checked after the three reads); otherwise it builds new_ka with the handler, the flags and siginitset of the first mask word. It then calls do_sigaction(sig, act ? &new_ka : NULL, oact ? &old_ka : NULL). If that returns 0 and oact is non-NULL it returns -EFAULT if access_ok(oact, sizeof(*oact)) fails or if any of the __put_user writes (sa_flags, sa_handler, sa_mask.sig[0], and zeros to sa_mask.sig[1], [2], [3]) fails; by then the new action has already been installed by do_sigaction. In every other case it returns the value returned by do_sigaction (0 or a negative errno). It takes no lock itself.
note: Macro-generated function; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 invocation (signal.c:81-118 in the slice). Old prose accurate; added that the -EFAULT on the oact copy comes after the new action was already installed.

name: kvm_mips_emulate_store
prose: Function kvm_mips_emulate_store(inst, cause, vcpu) emulating a trapped guest store as an MMIO write. curr_pc = vcpu->arch.pc is saved, then update_pc(vcpu, cause) is called; if it returns EMULATE_FAIL that value is returned with the PC as update_pc left it. Then run->mmio.phys_addr = kvm_mips_callbacks->gva_to_gpa(vcpu->arch.host_cp0_badvaddr) is stored; if it equals KVM_INVALID_ADDR the function jumps to out_fail (no error message is printed) leaving the invalid value in run->mmio.phys_addr. The opcode in inst selects the case: sd (CONFIG_64BIT), sw, sh and sb set run->mmio.len to 8, 4, 2 or 1 and store the low bytes of vcpu->arch.gprs[rt] into run->mmio.data; swl, swr (len 4, address rounded down to 4 bytes) and sdl, sdr (CONFIG_64BIT, len 8, address rounded down to 8 bytes) re-compute run->mmio.phys_addr from gva_to_gpa and merge bytes of the register into the existing data buffer according to the low address bits; on CONFIG_CPU_LOONGSON64 sdc2 takes rt from the Loongson format and for opcode1 0 to 3 stores 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes (len set accordingly), while for another opcode1 it only prints an error and then continues as below without changing run->mmio.len or data. Any other opcode prints "Store not yet supported" and jumps to out_fail. out_fail sets vcpu->arch.pc = curr_pc and returns EMULATE_FAIL (run->mmio.phys_addr stays as already written). On the other paths it sets vcpu->mmio_needed = 1, run->mmio.is_write = 1 and vcpu->mmio_is_write = 1 and calls kvm_io_bus_write(vcpu, KVM_MMIO_BUS, run->mmio.phys_addr, run->mmio.len, data); if that returns 0 it sets vcpu->mmio_needed = 0 and returns EMULATE_DONE, otherwise it returns EMULATE_DO_MMIO with mmio_needed left set.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the invalid-address path prints nothing and run->mmio.phys_addr has already been assigned (emulate.c:1000-1003 area, real file lines 968-1004); the same holds for the unsupported-opcode path. Old statement that the sdc2 bad-opcode path still does the bus write was right and kept. Slice cut the head; read the real file from line 969.

name: kvm_mips_complete_mmio_load
prose: Function kvm_mips_complete_mmio_load(vcpu) that finishes a guest load after userspace completed an MMIO read; it returns an emulation_result. It takes gpr = &vcpu->arch.gprs[vcpu->arch.io_gpr] and starts with er = EMULATE_DONE. If run->mmio.len is greater than sizeof(*gpr) (8) it logs "Bad MMIO length", returns EMULATE_FAIL and changes nothing else (the PC is not restored). Otherwise it sets vcpu->arch.pc = vcpu->arch.io_pc and switches on run->mmio.len: for 8, 4, 2 and 1 it writes *gpr from run->mmio.data according to vcpu->mmio_needed: for 8 bytes, values 11 to 17 and 20 to 26 merge parts of the loaded value with the old register contents (the unaligned ldl/ldr style cases) and any other value (including 18 and 19) stores the full signed 64-bit value; for 4 bytes, mmio_needed 1 zero-extends the 32-bit value, 2, 6 and 7 and any value not listed sign-extend it, and 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10 merge parts of it with the old register contents; for 2 and 1 bytes mmio_needed == 1 zero-extends and any other value sign-extends the loaded half-word or byte. For any other length (0, 3, 5, 6, 7) no register is written. It then returns er, which is EMULATE_DONE on all paths except the bad-length one. vcpu->mmio_needed is not changed by this function.
note: The listed name is an excerpt label: the slice cut the head, and the real function is kvm_mips_complete_mmio_load (mips/kvm/emulate.c:1509-1650); fixed under that name instead of dropping. Head read from the real file; the 8-byte cases 11-17 were read there.

name: kvm_irq_to_priority
prose: Function kvm_irq_to_priority(irq) that maps a hardware interrupt number to a KVM MIPS exception priority index. It loops i from MIPS_EXC_INT_TIMER up to but not including MIPS_EXC_MAX and returns the first i for which kvm_priority_to_irq[i] equals (1 << (irq + 8)), where kvm_priority_to_irq is the pointer variable currently in use (it defaults to kvm_default_priority_to_irq); if no entry matches it returns MIPS_EXC_MAX. The shift is done on an int, so it is only well-defined when irq + 8 is at most 30; irq values of 23 and above shift into or past the sign bit or beyond the width of int. It reads the table and writes nothing.
note: Contract cleared (global table). Reviewer round 15 right: for irq = 23 the shift 1 << 31 overflows a signed int, so the old precondition irq <= 23 was wrong. Round 1 (first match) is already stated. Slice 66-76.

name: kvm_vz_set_one_reg
prose: Static function kvm_vz_set_one_reg(vcpu, reg, v) that writes one guest CP0 or timer register selected by reg->id with the 64-bit value v. It returns -EINVAL with no state change if reg->id is not one handled here (default case), or if the guest lacks the feature required by the register: CONTEXTCONFIG and XCONTEXTCONFIG need cpu_guest_has_contextconfig; USERLOCAL needs cpu_guest_has_userlocal; SEGCTL0 to 2 need cpu_guest_has_segments; PWBASE, PWFIELD, PWSIZE and PWCTL need cpu_guest_has_htw or cpu_guest_has_ldpte; BADINSTR and BADINSTRP need their guest features; KSCRATCH1 to 6 need cpu_guest_has_kscr for that register; MAAR(n) and MAARI need cpu_guest_has_maar and require cpu_guest_has_dyn_maar to be false (so they also return -EINVAL when the guest has dynamic MAAR), and MAAR(n) also returns -EINVAL when n is at least ARRAY_SIZE(vcpu->arch.maar). Registers CONFIG1 to CONFIG5 are silently ignored (result 0) when the guest lacks that config level; PRID is silently ignored (result 0) on Octeon III; for CONFIG to CONFIG6 only the bits in the per-register user write mask can change (CONFIG1-5 are read and written through gc0, CONFIG6 through the software copy). Most other registers are written directly (some via helpers: COUNT with kvm_mips_write_count, COMPARE with kvm_mips_write_compare, WIRED with change_gc0_wired, CAUSE with ordering around the timer DC bit, EBASE with kvm_vz_write_gc0_ebase). For COUNT_CTL, COUNT_RESUME and COUNT_HZ it returns the result of kvm_mips_set_count_ctl, kvm_mips_set_count_resume or kvm_mips_set_count_hz respectively. In every other successful case it returns 0.
note: Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 right: MAAR and MAARI return -EINVAL also when cpu_guest_has_dyn_maar is set (vz.c slice lines 248 and 256); the old prose omitted it. The original rejection (CONFIG1-5 and PRID return 0, not -EINVAL) was already in the old prose. Slice cut the tail; the default case and final return ret were read from the real file (vz.c:2405-2408).

name: kvm_vz_gpsi_cop0
prose: Static function kvm_vz_gpsi_cop0(inst, opc, cause, vcpu) that emulates a guest COP0 instruction that raised a guest privileged sensitive instruction exception. It saves curr_pc = vcpu->arch.pc and calls update_pc(vcpu, cause); if that returns EMULATE_FAIL it returns EMULATE_FAIL immediately, without logging and without restoring the PC. Otherwise: if inst.co_format.co is set, a WAIT function returns the result of kvm_mips_emul_wait(vcpu) (which always returns EMULATE_DONE) and any other function leaves er = EMULATE_FAIL; if it is not set, the rs field selects a case. For mfc0 and dmfc0 it reads Count (kvm_mips_read_count), Compare, LLAddr (LLB bit only if cpu_guest_has_rw_llb, else 0), MAAR (selected by MAARI, with a BUG_ON if MAARI is out of range) and MAARI when the guest has MAAR and not dynamic MAAR, or the stored values of PRid, CDMMBase, CMGCRBase, SRSCtl, SRSMap, Config6, Config7 and ErrCtl (and Diag on CONFIG_CPU_LOONGSON64); any other register sets er = EMULATE_FAIL with val 0. If er is not EMULATE_FAIL the value (sign extended for mfc0) is stored in guest GPR rt. For mtc0 and dmtc0 it handles Count (after kvm_vz_lose_htimer), Compare, LLAddr (only clears LLB when cpu_guest_has_rw_llb and the written LLB bit is clear), MAAR, MAARI, Config6, ErrCtl (value ignored) and, on Loongson, Diag (flushing BTB, ITLB, DTLB, VTLB and FTLB according to the written bits, with local interrupts disabled); any other register gives EMULATE_FAIL. Any other rs value gives EMULATE_FAIL. At the end, if er is EMULATE_FAIL on these later paths it logs an error and restores vcpu->arch.pc = curr_pc; it then returns er (EMULATE_DONE on the handled paths).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the early update_pc failure returns without logging or PC restore, so the old text claiming every EMULATE_FAIL return logs and restores was wrong. Round 2 is wrong about the prose (it already said the PC is restored); round 1 (wait returns DONE without register update) is consistent with the prose. Slice cut the tail; the rest (Diag flush, default, final rollback and log) read from the real file lines 1020-1062.

name: pci_ehci_read_reg
prose: Function pci_ehci_read_reg(reg) returning the emulated 32-bit PCI configuration register value of the CS5536 EHCI controller for the offset reg (0 for any offset not listed below). It reads hardware MSRs for most registers and has one write side effect: for PCI_BAR0_REG it reads GLCP_SOFT_COM, and if SOFT_BAR_EHCI_FLAG is set it returns CS5536_EHCI_RANGE | PCI_BASE_ADDRESS_SPACE_MEMORY and clears that flag in the MSR with _wrmsr (so the soft-BAR value is returned once), otherwise it returns the USB_EHCI MSR low word masked with 0xfffff000. Other registers: PCI_VENDOR_ID returns the CS5536 EHCI device id and vendor id (low 16 bits 0x1022); PCI_COMMAND returns only the master and memory bits taken from the USB_EHCI MSR high word; PCI_STATUS returns 66MHz, fast-back and medium DEVSEL bits (0x2a0), plus the parity bit (0x3a0 total) if SB_PARE_ERR_FLAG is set in the SB_ERROR MSR; PCI_CLASS_REVISION returns the low byte of the USB_CAP MSR low word with CS5536_EHCI_CLASS_CODE in the upper 24 bits; PCI_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, PCI_CARDBUS_CIS, PCI_SUBSYSTEM_VENDOR_ID, PCI_ROM_ADDRESS, PCI_CAPABILITY_LIST and PCI_INTERRUPT_LINE return the constant values built from the CS5536 definitions; PCI_EHCI_LEGSMIEN_REG returns bits 16-21 of the USB_EHCI MSR high word, PCI_EHCI_LEGSMISTS_REG returns bits 24-29 of it, and PCI_EHCI_FLADJ_REG returns its bits 8-13 in place. It takes no lock.
note: Contract cleared (it depends on MSR reads and a write). Reviewer round 15 right: the old prose omitted the soft-BAR flag clearing side effect (cs5536_ehci.c slice 110-121). Rounds 1 and 2 concerned the contract only. Slice 75-156.

name: loongson2_cpu_set_rate
prose: Function loongson2_cpu_set_rate(rate_khz) that programs the clock-modulation field of the Loongson2 CHIPCFG register from loongson2_clockmod_table. It scans the table with cpufreq_for_each_valid_entry, which walks entries until the one whose frequency is CPUFREQ_TABLE_END and skips those whose frequency is CPUFREQ_ENTRY_INVALID, and stops at the first entry whose frequency equals rate_khz. If the scan ends without a match, pos is left at the terminator entry (frequency CPUFREQ_TABLE_END, driver_data DC_RESV). If rate_khz does not equal pos->frequency it returns -ENOTSUPP without touching the register. Otherwise it reads CHIPCFG with readl, replaces its low three bits with (pos->driver_data - 1) and writes it back with writel, and returns 0. The table here initialises the DC_25PT to DC_DISABLE entries with frequency 0, and the loongson2_cpufreq driver later overwrites them with real frequencies, so which rate_khz values succeed depends on the table contents at the time of the call; the terminator value itself also compares equal to the terminator entry.
note: Contract cleared (hardware register and mutable table). Reviewer round 1 is wrong about 4294967295 and terminator handling for the code as written (the scan stops at the terminator without skipping it, clock.c slice 39-43) but right that real frequencies are non-zero in practice, since drivers/cpufreq/loongson2_cpufreq.c:76-78 overwrites the table frequencies. The old numeric claims (only 0 and 4294967294 succeed) describe only the initial table and were removed. Slice 34-50.

name: register_loongson3_notifier
prose: Static function with no arguments, registered with early_initcall. It returns cpuhp_setup_state_nocalls(CPUHP_MIPS_SOC_PREPARE, "mips/loongson:prepare", loongson3_enable_clock, loongson3_disable_clock). That call installs loongson3_enable_clock as the startup callback and loongson3_disable_clock as the teardown callback for the CPUHP_MIPS_SOC_PREPARE hotplug state, to be called for later CPU bring-up and tear-down, and does not call them for CPUs that are already online. Because CPUHP_MIPS_SOC_PREPARE is a fixed (non-dynamic) state it returns 0 on success and a negative errno if the registration fails (in which case the callbacks are not installed). It takes no lock itself.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old prose said it returns the non-negative state number, but for a static state cpuhp_setup_state_nocalls returns 0 on success. Round 2 is wrong about the prose (it said no callbacks are registered only on failure). Slice 68-75.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(cacheflush, unsigned long, addr, unsigned long, bytes, unsigned int, cache)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_cacheflush (MIPS) taking addr, bytes and a cache selector that it does not use. If bytes is 0 it returns 0 without doing anything. Otherwise, if access_ok((void __user *)addr, bytes) fails it returns -EFAULT and flushes nothing. Otherwise it calls the function pointer __flush_icache_user_range(addr, addr + bytes) (instruction cache flush for the user range, through whatever implementation the CPU setup installed) and returns 0. These are its only three returns; it takes no lock.
note: Macro-generated function; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 invocation (cache.c:89-100). Old prose accurate; made explicit that the flush goes through the __flush_icache_user_range function pointer.

name: extract_dc
prose: Static function extract_dc(addr, data) of the SB1 cache-error handler, returning a uint32_t mask of CP0_CERRD_* flags describing problems found. It prints "Dcache index" and, for each of the 4 ways, performs an Index-load-tag-D cache operation at (way << 13) | addr and reads the tag registers; for way 0 it prints the bank, set and LRU order; it prints the way, physical address and tag state for every way. If the tag state is valid (DC_TAG_VALID) it checks the parity of PTag1 and PTag0 and, for each bad parity, prints a message and sets CP0_CERRD_TAG_ADDRESS in the result; if the state is not valid it sets CP0_CERRD_TAG_STATE. If data is non-zero it also, within each way, loads the four doublewords at offsets 0 to 3 with Index-load-data-D, computes dc_ecc on each, compares with the stored ECC byte and, on a mismatch, records it and sets CP0_CERRD_DATA_SBE when exactly one bit differs and CP0_CERRD_DATA_DBE otherwise; it prints the data and which doublewords have bad ECC. It returns the accumulated mask, which is 0 if nothing was flagged.
note: The listed item is a cut tail with a made-up name; the slice cut the head and the real function is extract_dc (cerr-sb1.c:~475-569). Fixed under that name instead of dropping. The old description covered only the data ECC part and omitted the tag parity and tag state flags.

name: prom_init
prose: Function prom_init() (an __init function with no arguments) that does early platform setup for MIPS Malta. It maps _pcictrl_bonito with ioremap(BONITO_REG_BASE, BONITO_REG_SIZE), reads mips_revision_corid, and if that is CORE_EMUL it refines it to EMUL_BON or EMUL_MSC by the Bonito PCIDID. It reads mips_revision_sconid and, if it is SCON_OTHER, derives it from the core id (GT64120, BONITO, SOCIT or ROCIT). It then switches on the system controller: GT64120 maps the GT registers, sets byte swapping in GT_PCI0_CMD, fixes the PCI I/O mapping if needed and calls set_io_port_base(MALTA_GT_PORT_BASE); BONITO maps the PCI config area, disables the IOBC, sets byte swapping and calls set_io_port_base(MALTA_BONITO_PORT_BASE); SOCIT and ROCIT map MIPS_MSC01_PCI_REG_BASE into _pcictrl_msc and SOCITSC and SOCITSCP map MIPS_SOCITSC_PCI_REG_BASE into _pcictrl_msc, after which these four share the MSC01 setup (barriers, PCI enable cleared, lane swap, BAR0, HEAD4 and P2SC mask/map registers written, target retries capped, the PCI config register written and set_io_port_base(MALTA_MSC_PORT_BASE)); any other controller value enters an endless loop (while (1);) and never returns. Then it sets board_nmi_handler_setup = mips_nmi_setup and board_ejtag_handler_setup = mips_ejtag_setup, calls fw_init_cmdline(), fw_meminit(), console_config() (only with CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE) and mips_cpc_probe(), and registers exactly one SMP ops set: register_cps_smp_ops() if it returns 0 (then returns), else register_vsmp_smp_ops() if it returns 0 (then returns), else register_up_smp_ops(). The mappings made with ioremap are never unmapped.
note: The listed item has an invented name; the slice cut the head, the real function is prom_init (malta-init.c:118-301). Fixed under that name. The old text described only the MSC01 branch and the tail; the GT64120 and Bonito branches and the corid/sconid detection were missing. Return paths: the two returns in the SMP registration (slice 39-42), the fall off the end after register_up_smp_ops, and the non-returning default case.

name: bcm63xx_setup_cfg_access
prose: Static function bcm63xx_setup_cfg_access(type, busn, devfn, where) that sets up the MPI for a PCI configuration cycle; busn is not used. It computes slot = PCI_SLOT(devfn), func = PCI_FUNC(devfn) and reg = where >> 2 (an unsigned value, so a negative where gives a very large reg). It returns 1 without any hardware access if slot is above (MPI_L2PCFG_DEVNUM_MASK >> MPI_L2PCFG_DEVNUM_SHIFT), or func is above (MPI_L2PCFG_FUNC_MASK >> MPI_L2PCFG_FUNC_SHIFT), or reg is above (MPI_L2PCFG_REG_MASK >> MPI_L2PCFG_REG_SHIFT). Otherwise it builds val from reg, func and slot shifted to their fields plus MPI_L2PCFG_CFG_USEREG_MASK and MPI_L2PCFG_CFG_SEL_MASK, adds 1 << MPI_L2PCFG_CFG_TYPE_SHIFT when type is non-zero, writes val to MPI_L2PCFG_REG with bcm_mpi_writel (no lock is taken here) and returns 0. The only returns are 1 and 0.
note: Contract cleared: the old contract depended on where alone (reviewer round 15 right that slot and func also cause the 1 return) and the function writes a hardware register. Round 2 (negative where) was already in the old prose. Slice 64-98.

name: __cvmx_pcie_rc_initialize_gen1
prose: Static function __cvmx_pcie_rc_initialize_gen1(pcie_port) that brings an Octeon PCIe gen1 root complex port from reset to a configured link; it has a retry label at its start. Return -1 (after a debug message, possibly after some registers were already written) if: port 0 is not in host mode (NPEI_CTL_STATUS.host_mode clear); on CN52XX port 1 is requested while qlm0_link_width shows it disabled; the port clock does not report running (checked via PESCX_CTL_STATUS2 pclk_run, except on CN56XX and CN52XX pass 1); PESCX_CTL_STATUS2 shows the port stuck in reset; PESCX_BIST_STATUS2 is non-zero; or __cvmx_pcie_rc_initialize_link_gen1 fails. Otherwise it: sets the switch arbitration and config retry fields in NPEI_CTL_STATUS (plus tag counts on CN52XX pass 1); brings the port (both ports on the EBH5200 board when pcie_port is 0) out of reset after a soft reset if needed with waits (udelay and a fixed __delay); a BIST failure in PESCX_BIST_STATUS is only printed; initialises config space and the link; sets the store-merge control; writes the memory-access SubDID entries 12 to 15 (port 0) or 16 to 19 (port 1); sets the peer-to-peer BAR start/end registers to -1; sets BAR0, BAR1 (16 index entries) and BAR2 start registers and the BAR2 attributes in NPEI_CTL_PORT0 or NPEI_CTL_PORT1; on CN52XX/CN56XX pass 1 and 2 it runs a workaround that writes to a test address, reads in/out FIFO counters, and if they are not aligned issues extra writes, calls cvmx_pcie_rc_initialize(0) when on the EBH5200 board with port 1, and jumps back to retry to redo the whole sequence; finally it prints the link width and returns 0.
note: Contract cleared (hardware CSR side effects). Prose checked against the real function: the listed -1 paths are right (pcie-octeon.c:697-1080). Added the retry loop and the BIST (non -2) failure that is only printed. Slice cut the head; the head was read from the real file.

name: ip22_gio_init
prose: Static __init function with no arguments that registers the SGI IP22 GIO bus and probes its slots. It calls device_register(&gio_bus); if that fails it calls put_device(&gio_bus) and returns the error. Otherwise it calls bus_register(&gio_bus_type); if that fails it calls device_unregister(&gio_bus) and returns the error. If bus_register succeeds it calls request_resource(&iomem_resource, &gio_bus_resource) ignoring the result, prints "GIO: Probing bus...", and probes the slots with ip22_check_gio: on a fullhouse machine (Indigo2) slots 0 and 1; otherwise slot 0 only if get_dbe on hpc3c1->pbdma[1] succeeds, and then slots 1 and 2. ip22_check_gio may allocate a struct gio_device with kzalloc and register it (an allocation failure for a slot just skips that slot), so devices and memory can remain allocated after a successful return. It then returns 0 (the value of bus_register). On success the bus device and bus type stay registered.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old statement that no memory is allocated was wrong because ip22_check_gio kzallocs a gio_device per detected slot and registers it (ip22-gio.c, ip22_check_gio). Round 1 (contract) concerns only the contract, which is empty. Slice 133-165.

name: xbow_probe
prose: Static function xbow_probe(nasid) that probes the xbow on a node. It finds the KLTYPE_MIDPLANE8 board in the node klconfig with find_lboard and returns -ENODEV if there is none; then finds the KLSTRUCT_XBOW component on it and returns -ENODEV if there is none. It then scans the xbow ports with a do-while loop (from the highest widget down if WIDGET_A is defined, else from the lowest up) for the first port that is both of hub type and enabled; this loop has no bound check, so it relies on such a port existing and would otherwise run past the table. That port becomes masterwid. If XBOW_PORT_NASID of that port is not nasid it returns 1 without probing. Otherwise it loops widget ids from HUB_WIDGET_ID_MIN to HUB_WIDGET_ID_MAX and, for each port that is enabled and of IO type, calls probe_one_port(nasid, i, masterwid) (its result is ignored), then returns 0. The only returns are -ENODEV, 1 and 0.
note: Contract cleared (reads klconfig and calls probe_one_port, and does not terminate without an enabled hub port). Old prose was accurate (reviewer round 15 only raised that the formal contract lacked the precondition). Slice 151-200.

name: heart_alloc_int
prose: Static inline function with no arguments that allocates a free interrupt bit from the shared bitmap heart_irq_map. It loops: bit = find_first_zero_bit(heart_irq_map, HEART_NUM_IRQS); if bit is not below HEART_NUM_IRQS it returns -ENOSPC without changing the bitmap; otherwise it calls test_and_set_bit(bit, heart_irq_map) and if that bit had already been set by someone else it retries from the search, else it returns bit, which this call has atomically set. It takes no lock; concurrent callers are handled by the atomic bit test-and-set and the retry.
note: Contract cleared (global bitmap state). Prose was accurate; reviewers rounds 1 and 15 only said the contract omitted ENOSPC. Slice 29-42.

name: arch_ptrace
prose: Function arch_ptrace(child, request, addr, data) for nios2 whose only statement returns ptrace_request(child, request, addr, data), i.e. the generic ptrace request handler is used for every request. The return value is whatever ptrace_request returns (0, a positive value such as PEEK data through the generic handler, or a negative errno). arch_ptrace itself does not take or release any lock or reference; ptrace_request may do so internally.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old claim that no locks, references or memory are acquired on behalf of the caller was too broad about the callee; the wrapper itself acquires none but ptrace_request may. Round 1 (positive PEEK results) already in the old prose. Slice 125-129.

name: do_signal
prose: Static function do_signal(regs) of nios2, returning an int restart code; it is called from do_notify_resume when TIF_SIGPENDING or TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL is set (so no real signal need be pending). It sets current->thread.kregs = regs. If regs->orig_r2 >= 0 and regs->r1 is non-zero (the entry came from a system call) it records continue_addr = regs->ea, restart_addr = continue_addr - 4 and retval = regs->r2; for ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK it sets restart to -1, for ERESTARTNOHAND, ERESTARTSYS and ERESTARTNOINTR to 1; for any of these four values it also sets regs->r2 = regs->orig_r2, regs->r7 = regs->orig_r7 and regs->ea = restart_addr; and it sets regs->orig_r2 = -1 whenever the entry came from a system call. Then if get_signal(&ksig) returns true: when restart is non-zero and regs->ea still equals restart_addr, for ERESTARTNOHAND or ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK, or for ERESTARTSYS with the handler lacking SA_RESTART, it sets regs->r2 = EINTR, regs->r7 = 1 and regs->ea = continue_addr (ERESTARTNOINTR and ERESTARTSYS with SA_RESTART keep the restart); it then calls handle_signal and returns 0. If no signal is delivered: when restart is non-zero and regs->ea equals restart_addr it sets regs->ea = continue_addr and regs->r2 = __NR_restart_syscall (for every restart kind); it calls restore_saved_sigmask() and returns restart (0 if no restart was prepared, 1, or -1).
note: Reviewer original (notify signal without a pending signal) right: the precondition is only that TIF_SIGPENDING or TIF_NOTIFY_SIGNAL is set. Round 15 right: EINTR conversion happens for ERESTARTNOHAND and ERESTART_RESTARTBLOCK regardless of SA_RESTART (slice 3-11). Round 2 about restart wording is not claimed here. Head read from the real file lines 235-268.

name: alloc_kuser_page
prose: Static function with no arguments, registered with arch_initcall, that sets up the nios2 kuser helper page. It computes kuser_sz from the linker symbols __kuser_helper_start and __kuser_helper_end and calls get_zeroed_page(GFP_ATOMIC); if that returns 0 it returns -ENOMEM and nothing else has changed (kuser_page[0] is untouched). Otherwise it copies kuser_sz bytes from __kuser_helper_start into the new page, calls flush_icache_range(vpage, vpage + KUSER_SIZE), stores virt_to_page(vpage) in kuser_page[0], and returns 0. The page is never freed by this function. The only returns are -ENOMEM and 0.
note: Contract cleared (global kuser_page and allocation; reviewers only objected that the formal contract omitted ENOMEM). Prose accurate; added GFP_ATOMIC, the flush length and that the page is not freed. Slice 76-93.

name: remap_area_pages
prose: Static function remap_area_pages(address, phys_addr, size, flags) that maps a kernel virtual range to physical memory in init_mm. end = address + size; phys_addr is made relative to address; it calls flush_cache_all(); if address >= end (size 0 or the range wraps) it calls BUG(). Otherwise it loops over page-directory slots (do-while, at least once): it sets error = -ENOMEM and allocates p4d, pud and pmd with p4d_alloc, pud_alloc and pmd_alloc, leaving the loop if any returns NULL; it calls remap_area_pmd for the part of the range in that slot and leaves the loop if that returns non-zero (it fails with -ENOMEM if a page table cannot be allocated, and its callee remap_area_pte calls BUG() if a page is already mapped in the range); otherwise it sets error = 0, advances address to the next page-directory boundary and moves dir on, continuing while address is non-zero and below end. It then calls flush_tlb_all() and returns error: 0 if every slot was mapped, -ENOMEM if an allocation or the pmd remap failed (earlier slots stay mapped and any allocated tables stay in place). It takes no lock itself.
note: Contract cleared (global kernel page tables). Prose verified against remap_area_pmd and remap_area_pte in the real file (ioremap.c:21-74); the already-mapped BUG is in remap_area_pte, not in this function, and the cache flush happens before the size check. Slice 76-112.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add, +=)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v) (static __inline__ void, from ATOMIC_OP(add, +=) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add, +=)). It saves interrupts with _atomic_spin_lock_irqsave, which on CONFIG_SMP also takes the arch spinlock selected by ATOMIC_HASH(v) (one of 4 locks chosen from the address divided by L1_CACHE_BYTES) and on uniprocessor builds only disables local interrupts; executes v->counter += i; releases the lock if taken and restores the saved interrupt state with _atomic_spin_unlock_irqrestore; and returns nothing. The same ATOMIC_OPS invocation also defines arch_atomic_add_return and arch_atomic_fetch_add, which are separate functions not described here.

name: kprobe_ftrace_handler
prose: Ftrace callback for kprobes on parisc (built with CONFIG_KPROBES_ON_FTRACE), taking ip, parent_ip, ops and fregs; it returns nothing. It returns at once, without touching the recursion lock, if kprobe_ftrace_disabled is set or if ftrace_test_recursion_trylock(ip, parent_ip) returns a negative value. Otherwise the recursion lock is held until the single exit label out, where ftrace_test_recursion_unlock is called. It gets regs from fregs and looks up the kprobe p at ip with get_kprobe; if there is none or it is disabled it goes to out. If kprobe_running() is true on this CPU it increments the missed count of p (the kprobe found for this ip, not the running one) with kprobes_inc_nmissed_count and goes to out, leaving current_kprobe unchanged. Otherwise it stores p in the per-cpu current_kprobe, sets the control block status to KPROBE_HIT_ACTIVE and sets regs->iaoq to {ip, ip + 4}; if p has no pre_handler or the pre_handler returns 0 it sets regs->iaoq to {ip + 4, ip + 8} and, if p has a post_handler, sets the status to KPROBE_HIT_SSDONE and calls it with 0; if the pre_handler returns non-zero the iaoq values stay {ip, ip + 4} and the post_handler is not called. In every case of this last path current_kprobe is then set to NULL before out.
note: Old prose said the missed count of the already-running kprobe is incremented; the code increments the count of p (ftrace.c slice line 222). Rest of the old prose checked and kept; reviewer original/round 2 points (lock release, trylock failure path) are covered in the new wording. Slice 201-246.

name: handle_interruption
prose: Function handle_interruption(code, regs) (notrace) that handles a PA-RISC interruption; it returns nothing. It first enables local interrupts if the saved PSW in regs->gr[0] had them enabled. If (regs->iaoq[0] & 3) is non-zero and regs->iasq[0] differs from regs->sr[7] it rewrites iaoq[0] to PRIV_USER, iaoq[1] to iaoq[0] + 4, both iasq entries to sr[7], clears PSW_B in gr[0], and returns. Otherwise it switches on code: 1 (HPMC) sends a chassis status and calls parisc_terminate (does not return); 2 prints a power-failure message and returns; 3 clears PSW_R, passes single-step to kgdb when configured, calls handle_gdb_break(TRAP_TRACE) for a user-space fault, and returns; 5 (LPMC) sends a chassis status, flushes caches and TLB, calls default_trap(code, regs) and returns; 8, 10 and 11 (illegal instruction, privileged operation, privileged register) call die_if_kernel and then force SIGILL at iaoq[0], except that code 11 for the MFCTL cr26/cr27 instruction pattern is emulated by writing the GR and advancing iaoq, then returning; 9 calls handle_break and returns; 12 forces SIGFPE (FPE_INTOVF); 13 forces SIGFPE (FPE_CONDTRAP) for user mode and returns, while in kernel mode it leaves the switch; 14 calls die_if_kernel, updates statistics and calls handle_fpe, then returns; 18 calls handle_unaligned and returns if check_unaligned succeeds, else behaves like 26; 19 sets PSW_X and, like 21, calls handle_gdb_break(TRAP_HWBKPT) and returns; 25 clears PSW_T, calls handle_gdb_break(TRAP_BRANCH) for user space and returns; 28 calls handle_unaligned and returns; 7 for user mode takes the mmap read lock, looks up the vma at iaoq[0] and, if it exists and has VM_EXEC, sets fault_address = iaoq[0], fault_space = iasq[0], releases the lock and leaves the switch for the page-fault path, otherwise releases the lock, sets regs->iir = 0xbaadf00d and continues as code 27; 27 (and 7) returns after fixup_exception for kernel-mode code 27, else die_if_kernel and a SIGSEGV (SEGV_MAPERR at iaoq[0] for code 7, at ior otherwise); any other code in user mode forces SIGBUS (BUS_OBJERR) at ior and returns, and in kernel mode sends a chassis panic status and calls parisc_terminate. The cases that leave the switch are the instruction TLB trap (fault_address = iaoq[0], fault_space = iasq[0]), codes 15, 16 and 17 (code 17 first returns if handle_nadtlb_fault succeeds; then fault_address = ior, fault_space = isr), 18 falling into 26 (ior, isr), 7 with an executable vma, and code 13 in kernel mode (both stay 0). On that path: for user mode, if the space id of fault_space differs from that of sr[7] it prints a message, forces SIGSEGV (SEGV_MAPERR at ior) and returns; for kernel mode, if faulthandler_disabled() or fault_space is 0 it returns if fixup_exception or kfence_handle_page_fault handles it, otherwise sends a chassis panic status and calls parisc_terminate("Kernel Fault"); finally it calls do_page_fault(regs, code, fault_address).
note: Reviewer round 2 and 15 right: the old prose omitted code 5 (LPMC), which returns after default_trap, and did not note that the code 7 and 27 kernel-mode path goes through die_if_kernel. The original rejection (code 13 in kernel mode reaching the page-fault code with fault_address/space 0) is right and kept. Slice cut head and tail; read the real file lines 477-801.

name: decode_fpu
prose: Function decode_fpu(Fpu_register, trap_counts) of the parisc FPU emulator, called after an FP exception trap, returning a u_int that is 0 (NOTRAP) or SIGNALCODE(sig, code) = (sig << 24) | code. Fpu_register is the FP register image (word 0 is the status word, words 1 to 7 are the exception registers, and the data registers are indexed up to 2 * 31 + 1 = 63 by the target field, so it must hold 64 words); trap_counts is passed to update_trap_counts but the macro does not use it. At entry the five high bits of word 0 are saved in bflags and cleared; every return path goes through update_trap_counts, which stores aflags = word0 >> 27 and ORs bflags back into word 0. Flow: (1) if the T-bit is clear it returns SIGNALCODE(SIGILL, ILL_COPROC) (reserved-op exception). (2) Otherwise it examines exception registers 1 to MAX_EXCP_REG (7) in turn: for an unimplemented-type exception it clears the T-bit and that register, calls fpudispatch to emulate; if that returns a non-zero exception it sets the T-bit again and rewrites the register, and if it is UNIMPLEMENTEDEXCEPTION returns SIGNALCODE(SIGILL, ILL_COPROC), else continues with the new type; if fpudispatch reports NOEXCEPTION it breaks out of the loop. (3) For an underflow exception: with the underflow trap enabled it returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTUND); otherwise it computes the default (denormalised) result into the target register (undoing round-away first), sets the underflow flag if inexact, and if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled rewrites the register to an inexact exception and returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTRES), else clears the register, sets the inexact flag if inexact, and continues with the next register. (4) Otherwise it switches on the type: overflow or overflow with inexact: with the overflow trap enabled returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTOVF); else sets the default overflow result, sets the overflow flag and, if the inexact trap is enabled, rewrites the register as an inexact exception and returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTRES), else clears the register and sets the inexact flag; invalid (including the opcode 2E variant) returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTINV) leaving the register; division by zero clears the register and returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTDIV); inexact returns SIGNALCODE(SIGFPE, FPE_FLTRES); an unknown type prints a message and returns SIGNALCODE(SIGILL, ILL_COPROC); no exception clears the register. (5) If the loop ends (or breaks) with no signal returned it clears the T-bit and returns 0. On the trapping returns the T-bit and, except for division by zero, the scanned exception register are left as they were.
note: Reviewer original and round 2 right: the trap returns leave the T-bit and exception register as set by hardware (old prose said some of these were cleared). Round 15 right: target * 2 + 1 reaches word 63, so the old at-least-15-words precondition was wrong. Slice cut the tail; the rest was read from the real file (decode_exc.c:90-330). Within the overflow case update_trap_counts is invoked twice on the trap path; harmless.

name: dbl_fdiv
prose: Function dbl_fdiv(srcptr1, srcptr2, dstptr, status) that divides the double at srcptr1 by the double at srcptr2 and stores the result at dstptr (it is the IEEE divide of the parisc FPU emulator). The result sign is the XOR of the operand signs. Special operands, in order: if operand 1 is infinity: when operand 2 is not a NaN, infinity divided by infinity is invalid (returns INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, otherwise it sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION) and infinity divided by anything else stores a signed infinity and returns NOEXCEPTION; if operand 1 is a NaN: a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, otherwise sets the invalid flag and quiets it; else if operand 2 is a signaling NaN the same trap-or-quiet rule applies to it and operand 2 is stored; otherwise operand 1 (quiet NaN) is stored; each ends with NOEXCEPTION. If operand 2 is infinity: a finite operand 1 gives a signed zero; if it is a NaN the same quiet/trap rule applies and operand 2 is stored; NOEXCEPTION. If operand 2 is zero: 0/0 is invalid (trap, or flag and quiet NaN stored, NOEXCEPTION); a non-zero operand 1 returns DIVISIONBYZEROEXCEPTION if that trap is enabled, else sets the division-by-zero flag, stores a signed infinity and returns NOEXCEPTION. Then dest_exponent = exp1 - exp2 + DBL_BIAS; a zero operand 1 stores a signed zero and returns NOEXCEPTION; denormal operands are normalised with dest_exponent adjusted; the mantissas are divided with a non-restoring algorithm for up to DBL_P quotient bits, giving a guard bit and sticky bit (inexact is guard OR sticky), and when inexact and (dest_exponent > 0 or the underflow trap is enabled) the mantissa is rounded according to the current rounding mode (ROUNDPLUS, ROUNDMINUS or ROUNDNEAREST) with the exponent incremented if the hidden bit overflows. Finalisation (after rounding, with dest_exponent the result exponent): if dest_exponent >= DBL_INFINITY_EXPONENT (overflow) and the overflow trap is enabled it stores the result with a wrapped exponent (Dbl_setwrapped_exponent) at dstptr and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION, or OVERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION when the result is inexact and the inexact trap is enabled (if inexact but the trap is disabled it sets the inexact flag and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION); with the overflow trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, replaces the result by the overflow value (infinity or largest finite per the rounding mode) and treats it as inexact. If dest_exponent <= 0 (underflow) and the underflow trap is enabled it stores the wrapped-exponent result and returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION, or UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION with the same inexact rules as for overflow; with the trap disabled it denormalises the mantissa (or produces zero), applies the rounding increment for the rounding mode when inexact, and sets the underflow flag only if the result is inexact and tiny. Otherwise it stores dest_exponent in the result. It then stores the result at dstptr and, if inexact, returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled and otherwise sets the inexact flag; the last return is NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.
note: Listed name dbl_round_finalize is not a function: the slice is the tail of dbl_fdiv, so it is fixed under the real name (dfdiv.c:36-387) after reading the head from the real file. The invalid/trap returns (INVALIDEXCEPTION, DIVISIONBYZEROEXCEPTION) do not store a result.

name: dbl_fmpy
prose: Function dbl_fmpy(srcptr1, srcptr2, dstptr, status) that multiplies the doubles at srcptr1 and srcptr2 and stores the result at dstptr. The result sign is the XOR of the operand signs. Special operands, in order: if operand 1 is infinity: when operand 2 is not a NaN, infinity times zero is invalid (INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else it sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION) and infinity times any other value stores a signed infinity and returns NOEXCEPTION; if operand 1 is a NaN: a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, otherwise sets the invalid flag and quiets it; else if operand 2 is a signaling NaN the same trap-or-quiet rule applies to it and operand 2 is stored; otherwise operand 1 is stored; each ends with NOEXCEPTION. If operand 2 is infinity: with operand 1 zero it is invalid (trap, or flag and a quiet NaN built from operand 2 stored, NOEXCEPTION); otherwise a signed infinity is stored; if operand 2 is a NaN the quiet/trap rule applies and operand 2 is stored; NOEXCEPTION. Then dest_exponent = exp1 + exp2 - DBL_BIAS; a zero operand 1 or operand 2 stores a signed zero and returns NOEXCEPTION; denormal operands are normalised with dest_exponent adjusted; the mantissas are multiplied with a shift-and-add loop that handles four bits per pass over DBL_P bits, collecting a sticky bit and a guard bit (inexact is guard OR sticky), the product is normalised (dest_exponent adjusted), and when inexact and (dest_exponent > 0 or the underflow trap is enabled) it is rounded according to the current rounding mode with the exponent incremented if the hidden bit overflows. Finalisation (after rounding, with dest_exponent the result exponent): if dest_exponent >= DBL_INFINITY_EXPONENT (overflow) and the overflow trap is enabled it stores the result with a wrapped exponent (Dbl_setwrapped_exponent) at dstptr and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION, or OVERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION when the result is inexact and the inexact trap is enabled (if inexact but the trap is disabled it sets the inexact flag and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION); with the overflow trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, replaces the result by the overflow value (infinity or largest finite per the rounding mode) and treats it as inexact. If dest_exponent <= 0 (underflow) and the underflow trap is enabled it stores the wrapped-exponent result and returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION, or UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION with the same inexact rules as for overflow; with the trap disabled it denormalises the mantissa (or produces zero), applies the rounding increment for the rounding mode when inexact, and sets the underflow flag only if the result is inexact and tiny. Otherwise it stores dest_exponent in the result. It then stores the result at dstptr and, if inexact, returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled and otherwise sets the inexact flag; the last return is NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.
note: Listed name dbl_round_and_pack is not a function: the slice is the tail of dbl_fmpy (dfmpy.c:36-381), fixed under the real name after reading the head from the real file. The invalid-trap return does not store a result.

name: dbl_fsub
prose: Function dbl_fsub(leftptr, rightptr, dstptr, status) that computes left - right in double precision and stores the result at dstptr (the listed name dbl_fadd is not in the source: the file is dfsub.c). Special operands, in order: if left is infinity: when right is not a NaN, infinity minus an infinity of the same sign is invalid (INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN, returns NOEXCEPTION) and otherwise left is stored as the result (NOEXCEPTION); if left is a NaN, a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag and quiets it; else if right is a signaling NaN the same rule applies and right is stored; otherwise left is stored; each ends with NOEXCEPTION. If right is infinity the result is right with its sign inverted (NOEXCEPTION); if right is a NaN the quiet/trap rule applies and right is stored (NOEXCEPTION). For finite operands it orders them by magnitude (swapping and inverting the sign as needed) so left is not smaller, then: if right is zero and left is zero the result is zero with its sign chosen from the signs by the rounding mode (ROUNDMINUS ORs the signs, other modes AND them) and NOEXCEPTION; if right is zero and left is not, left is the exact result (NOEXCEPTION), except that a denormal left with the underflow trap enabled is normalised and returned with a wrapped exponent and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION; if both are denormal the sum or difference is computed exactly: a zero difference is stored as zero (negative for ROUNDMINUS) with NOEXCEPTION, a sum that became normal is stored with NOEXCEPTION, otherwise with the underflow trap enabled the normalised wrapped result is stored and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned, else the result is stored and NOEXCEPTION returned. Otherwise it aligns right (shift limited to DBL_THRESHOLD) into an extension word and subtracts or adds the magnitudes depending on the signs. For a difference it renormalises: an exact zero result is stored (negative for ROUNDMINUS) with NOEXCEPTION; if the exponent falls to 0 or below it returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION with a wrapped exponent when the underflow trap is enabled, otherwise it returns the exact denormalised result with NOEXCEPTION; when renormalisation finishes with a valid exponent the result is stored and the function returns NOEXCEPTION unless the extension holds non-zero bits, in which case it goes on to rounding. For a sum it shifts right by one if the hidden overflow bit is set and increments the exponent. Rounding: if the extension is non-zero the result is inexact and is rounded by the current rounding mode (nearest-even, up, down, or truncate); the exponent is incremented if the hidden bit overflows. If the result exponent equals DBL_INFINITY_EXPONENT (overflow) and the overflow trap is enabled it stores the wrapped result and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION (or OVERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled, else sets the inexact flag); with the trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, stores the overflow value (infinity or largest finite) and treats it as inexact. Otherwise it stores the exponent. It stores the result at dstptr and, if inexact, returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled else sets the inexact flag; the last return is NOEXCEPTION.
note: Slice is the tail of dbl_fsub (the listed name dbl_fadd belongs to a different file and is not present in dfsub.c); fixed under the real name after reading the head (dfsub.c:36-513). Prose is a summary of the paths that determine the return value; the bit-level shift counts are not restated.

name: dbl_to_sgl_fcnvff
prose: Function dbl_to_sgl_fcnvff(srcptr, _nullptr, dstptr, status) converting a double at srcptr to a single stored at dstptr (the second parameter is unused). The sign is copied. If the source exponent is the infinity exponent: an infinity gives a single infinity stored with NOEXCEPTION; a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag and quiets it; the NaN (now quiet) is stored as a single NaN built from the high mantissa bits (forced to a quiet NaN if the truncated mantissa would be zero) and NOEXCEPTION is returned. Otherwise it converts the exponent; if the single exponent is not positive and the source is zero it stores a signed zero and returns NOEXCEPTION; the mantissa is converted (using the denormalising conversion that records is_tiny when the underflow trap is disabled and the single exponent is not positive), giving inexact, guard and sticky bits, and when inexact the mantissa is rounded according to the rounding mode. After rounding, a hidden-bit overflow increments dest_exponent when dest_exponent > 0 or the underflow trap is enabled. Then: if dest_exponent >= SGL_INFINITY_EXPONENT: with the overflow trap enabled it returns UNIMPLEMENTEDEXCEPTION without storing if dest_exponent >= SGL_INFINITY_EXPONENT + SGL_WRAP, else stores a wrapped-exponent result and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION (| INEXACTEXCEPTION when inexact and the inexact trap is enabled; if inexact with the trap disabled the inexact flag is set); with the trap disabled it sets the overflow flag and the overflow result and treats it as inexact. If dest_exponent <= 0: with the underflow trap enabled it returns UNIMPLEMENTEDEXCEPTION if dest_exponent <= -SGL_WRAP, else stores a wrapped result and returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION (| INEXACTEXCEPTION on the same rule); with the trap disabled it sets the underflow flag when the result is inexact and tiny. Otherwise it stores dest_exponent. Finally it stores the result at dstptr and returns INEXACTEXCEPTION if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled; if inexact with the trap disabled it sets the inexact flag; the last return is NOEXCEPTION.

name: dbl_to_dbl_fcnvfut
prose: Function dbl_to_dbl_fcnvfut(srcptr, _nullptr, dstptr, status) converting the double at srcptr to a 64-bit unsigned integer at dstptr (second parameter unused). src_exponent = exponent - DBL_BIAS. If src_exponent > DBL_FX_MAX_EXP + 1 (overflow, including infinity and NaN): the result is 0 for a sign-set source and all ones otherwise; it returns INVALIDEXCEPTION without writing if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag, writes the result and returns NOEXCEPTION. Otherwise if src_exponent >= 0: for a sign-set source the result is 0 with the same invalid trap/flag handling (INVALIDEXCEPTION without writing, or write and NOEXCEPTION); for a positive source it writes the mantissa shifted by src_exponent (truncation toward zero) and, if bits were lost, returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled (the result already written) or sets the inexact flag. If src_exponent < 0 it writes 0 and, if the source is non-zero (including denormals), returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled or sets the inexact flag. The last return is NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.
